A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same pragmatics survey and support comparison of the complete text, references, figures and appendices. V1's Appendix A is retained and expanded; v2 adds Appendix B and Table 1.

before.justification: Section 6.1 reports the authors' own descriptive analysis of surveyed resources: 11 of 57 papers, approximately 19%, include non-English languages. This qualifies as original data analysis, although the model experiments discussed belong to cited studies.

after.justification: V2 retains the original survey-corpus analysis in Section 6.1 and provides a joint classification in Appendix B. The inconsistent corpus totals do not negate the presence of original descriptive results.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an original algorithm or model. The retained bottom-up and top-down dataset-construction discussion describes prior work; its additional examples do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: No datasets, tasks or scenarios are added for original model training or evaluation. The added manner-implicature and discourse-marker resources expand the literature review.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed method against baselines. Newly cited studies do not participate in an original comparative experiment.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes the stated survey sample from 57 to 55 papers, a limited reported sample-size revision. The search cutoff remains December 31, 2024. Section 6.1 still uses 57, so v2 does not consistently specify its analyzed corpus.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, error analyses or experimental case studies are added. Appendix B cross-references the literature classifications already organized around phenomena and tasks.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run procedures, confidence intervals or significance tests for its own analysis. The new discussion of human label variation introduces no statistical estimation or uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The survey's classification entries change: Figure 2 adds Sap et al. (2020) under question answering and removes Westera et al. (2020a) from multiple-choice questions. Figures 1–2 also incorporate newly reviewed studies. No original model-performance measurements are added.

T1.justification: The linguistic concepts remain substantively unchanged, and neither version supplies mathematical theorems or proofs. The added scalar-pair examples in Section 4.2 are explanatory illustrations.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions: organizing pragmatic-evaluation resources, identifying gaps and recommending richer benchmarks. The introduction's added section roadmap does not change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 adds demographic bias and subjective annotation variation as evaluation concerns. The Limitations section newly acknowledges the survey's restricted multimodal coverage, and Section 6.4 qualifies the potential of LLM-generated experimental stimuli.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds the rationale for choosing ACL Anthology, three inclusion criteria, terminology-sensitive manual screening and supplementation from other sources. These improve documentation of survey selection without establishing that each disclosed procedure is newly introduced.

R1.justification: V2 adds literature on manner implicature, discourse markers, human label variation, synthetic data and linguistic contributions to LLM development. It removes Westera et al.'s distinct 'Similarity or deeper understanding?' paper while retaining their other TED-Q paper. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes local language corrections, clarifies examples, expands Appendix A and acknowledgements, and adds Appendix B. The main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 retain their tree structures but use more compact layouts and updated reference boxes. The new full-page Table 1 displays task-to-phenomenon relationships across the existing categories.

improvement.justification: Clearer selection criteria, fuller literature coverage, the task-to-phenomenon table and additional scope qualifications modestly improve the survey's usefulness and transparency. V2 introduces a reporting inconsistency: Appendix A states 55 papers while Section 6.1 retains 57. This limits numerical reliability, but the documentation and synthesis gains support a modest net improvement.
